title: Auth methods
lead: Every way a client can exchange an identity for a Tuck token: AppRole for machines, JWT/OIDC for CI and SSO, LDAP for people, Kubernetes for pods. Each role maps an identity to policies.

error.title: Could not load
error.message: The server did not answer as expected.

forbidden.title: This token cannot read the auth methods
forbidden.text: The server refused the request. Ask an administrator to extend your policy, then retry.

f.name: Role name
f.nameTaken: A role with this name already exists. Open it to edit.
f.nsHint: Tokens are issued in this namespace. Empty = root.
f.policiesHint: Enter or comma adds a policy.

approle.title: AppRole roles
approle.text: A client logs in with a role_id plus a one-time secret_id that you issue here.
approle.gone: Hidden. Issue a new secret_id if you need one.
approle.noSecret: The secret_id is never stored. Issue one to see it here for 60 seconds.

f.regenHint: Clients using the old role_id will stop logging in.

drawer.hint: Saving keeps the current role_id unless you ask to regenerate it.

delete.title: Delete AppRole role
delete.msg: Role {{name}} and its role_id stop working immediately. Type the name to confirm.

jwt.text: Tuck verifies incoming JWTs against the provider's jwks_uri, then picks a role by its bound claims.

noCfg.title: No provider configured yet
noCfg.text: Fill in jwks_uri below and save. Until then JWT logins are rejected.

f.jwksHint: Where the signing keys are published.
f.defaultTtlHint: Token lifetime for roles that set none. 0 = server default.
f.audsHint: Enter adds a value. Token aud must match one.
f.claimsHint: Every listed claim must equal its value.
f.groupsHint: Enter adds a group. The token's groups claim must contain at least one of them.

sso.title: SSO sign-in (optional)
sso.text: Turns on the "Sign in with SSO" button on the login page (authorization code + PKCE). Leave empty for JWT-only. With SSO on, set bound_groups or bound_claims on roles: a role with no bounds matches every user of the provider.
sso.authUrlHint: The provider's authorization endpoint. https only (http is allowed for localhost).
sso.tokenUrlHint: Where the authorization code is exchanged for a token.
sso.clientIdHint: The client ID registered for Tuck at the provider. Also the default id_token audience.
sso.secretHint: Leave empty for a public client (PKCE only).
sso.secretSet: A secret is stored and never shown. Leave empty to keep it.
sso.secretClearing: The secret will be removed on save.
sso.redirectHint: Must match what is registered at the provider: https://<host>/ui/auth/oidc/callback.
sso.scopesHint: Space-separated; openid is always added. Groups usually need the groups scope.

jwt.replaceNote: Saving replaces the whole provider config.
jwt.rolesText: A role binds claims to policies and a namespace.

drawer.hint: Leave the bindings empty to accept any valid token from the provider.

delete.title: Delete JWT role
delete.msg: Role {{name}} stops accepting logins immediately. Type the name to confirm.

ldap.text: Users sign in with their directory password; users and groups on a role decide the policies.

noCfg.title: No directory configured yet
noCfg.text: Add a server URL and a user_dn below and save.

f.urlsNone: Add at least one ldap:// or ldaps:// URL.
f.urlsHint: Enter adds a server. Tried in order.
f.bindDnHint: Service account used to search. Optional.
f.bindPwHint: Leave as is to keep the current password.
f.groupFilterHint: LDAP filter used to find a user's groups.
f.caCertHint: PEM of the CA that signed the directory certificate (your internal CA). Empty = system trust store.
f.usersHint: Enter or comma adds a login.
f.groupsHint: Group DNs contain commas, so only Enter adds one.
f.membersNone: No users or groups: this role matches nobody.

insecureWarn.title: Certificate checks are off
insecureWarn.text: Anyone able to intercept the connection can read directory passwords.

plainWarn.title: Plain ldap:// without StartTLS
plainWarn.text: Passwords travel unencrypted. Use ldaps:// or enable starttls.

ldap.replaceNote: Saving replaces the whole directory config.
ldap.rolesText: A role maps users and groups to policies.

drawer.hint: Users and groups are matched against the directory at login.

delete.title: Delete LDAP role
delete.msg: Role {{name}} stops accepting logins immediately. Type the name to confirm.

k8s.text: A pod sends its service-account JWT; Tuck has the cluster verify it with a TokenReview, then looks up the role for that namespace/serviceAccount. The animation is a schema, not live traffic.
k8s.clustersText: The default cluster plus every extra one declared in the server config. Pick one to look roles up in.

addCluster.title: Adding a cluster
addCluster.text: Clusters are declared in the Tuck server configuration, not from the UI. Restart the server after changing it.

k8s.rolesText: One role per namespace and service account.
k8s.found: Role {{ns}}/{{sa}} found and added to the table.
k8s.notFound: No role for {{ns}}/{{sa}} in this cluster.
k8s.noList: The server cannot list Kubernetes roles, so the table shows only roles you looked up or saved in this session.
k8s.empty: Look a role up to see it here.

drawer.hint: Namespace and service account identify the role and cannot be changed later.

delete.title: Delete Kubernetes role
delete.msg: Pods running as {{name}} in {{cluster}} lose access. Type the service account name to confirm.

step.0: Pod reads its service-account JWT and calls login.
step.1: Tuck receives the JWT and the requested role.
step.2: Tuck asks the cluster to run a TokenReview.
step.3: Tuck looks up the role for namespace/serviceAccount.
step.4: Tuck issues a token carrying the role's policies.

verdict.idleText: Press replay to walk through the sequence.
verdict.okText: The pod can now read secrets its policies allow.
verdict.noText: No role for this service account, so no token is issued.

flow.note: Tokens are placeholders; this view never shows real credentials or measurements.

token.title: Token auth
token.text: Tokens are the base credential every other method ends in. Create, look up and revoke them on the Tokens screen.
token.always: This method cannot be disabled or configured.
